questions.q: Who does most of the cooking in your family?
questions.answer: My mother, without a doubt. She's an excellent cook and takes real pride in it. My younger sister and I help occasionally, but honestly, nobody can [[replicate]] her fish curry, no matter how hard we try.

I do, actually, though I only really cook at the weekend. During the week I'm too busy, but on a lazy Saturday I quite enjoy trying a new recipe. I find the whole process rather [[therapeutic]] after a hectic week.

Nothing too ambitious. I can make a decent chicken curry, khichuri and simple fried fish. Lately I've been trying to [[master]] a proper biryani, although my first attempts were fairly disappointing, to put it kindly.
Surprisingly, yes. When I'm not rushed, following a recipe and getting fully [[immersed]] in it takes my mind off everything else. And of course there's the reward of a good meal at the end.

questions.q: Do you think children should learn to cook?
questions.answer: Definitely. Cooking is a basic life skill, and it teaches children about nutrition and independence. If they learn early, they're far less likely to [[fall back on]] fast food when they eventually live on their own.
